title: Retracing and rewriting the evolutionary trajectories of mammalian developmental enhancers
authors: Li T; Lalanne J; Kajiwara EA; Jain S; Li X; Do TV; Martin BK; Regalado SG; Daza RM; Shendure J
one_liner_zh: 该文利用深度学习预测染色质可及性并结合MPRA实验，追踪哺乳动物增强子的进化轨迹并识别关键TFBS突变，虽聚焦增强子而非直接建模TF-DNA互作，但方法可迁移至TF-DNA结合位点预测与机制研究。
abstract:
ABSTRACT

Cis -regulatory elements (CREs) such as enhancers play a central role in orchestrating mammalian development, yet how they have gained, lost, maintained or changed function over the course of mammalian evolution remains poorly understood. To address this gap, we densely mapped the functional evolution of five mouse developmental enhancers by testing orthologous sequences from 480 extant and ancestrally reconstructed mammalian genomes (Zoonomia 1 , Cactus 2 ) with massively parallel reporter assays (MPRAs). This phylogenetic dissection revealed diverse modes of evolution, from lineage-restricted activity to deep functional conservation despite extensive sequence divergence. To pinpoint causal changes, we developed a model-driven reconstitution strategy that uses deep learning-based predictions of chromatin accessibility to re-introduce a succession of mutations into ancestral orthologs; this revealed critical transcription factor binding site (TFBS) changes and pervasive context-dependent epistasis, including instances where mutational effects were strongly contingent on the order of their introduction. When we extended this strategy to tune the activity of extant orthologs, we found that ablation of enhancer function required as few as one to seven mutations, whereas enhancement was constrained by element-specific activity ceilings—a striking asymmetry in the predictability of model-guided enhancer editing. Together, these results shed light on how the plasticity of mammalian enhancers intersects with their evolution, and advance a framework for reprogramming the activity of endogenous CREs at nucleotide resolution.
abstract_zh:
摘要

顺式调控元件（cis-regulatory elements, CREs），如增强子，在协调哺乳动物发育中发挥核心作用，然而它们在哺乳动物进化过程中如何获得、丢失、维持或改变功能仍知之甚少。为填补这一空白，我们通过测试来自480个现存及祖先重建哺乳动物基因组（Zoonomia 1 , Cactus 2 ）的直系同源序列，并结合大规模平行报告分析（massively parallel reporter assays, MPRAs），密集绘制了五个小鼠发育增强子的功能进化图谱。这种系统发育剖析揭示了多样化的进化模式，从谱系限制性活性到尽管序列高度分歧但功能深度保守。为精确定位因果变化，我们开发了一种模型驱动的重构策略，利用基于深度学习的染色质可及性预测，将一系列突变重新引入祖先直系同源序列；这揭示了关键转录因子结合位点（transcription factor binding site, TFBS）的变化以及普遍存在的背景依赖性上位效应，包括突变效应强烈依赖于其引入顺序的实例。当我们将此策略扩展至调节现存直系同源序列的活性时，发现消除增强子功能仅需少至一至七个突变，而增强则受元件特异性活性上限的约束——这在模型引导的增强子编辑可预测性中呈现出显著的不对称性。综上，这些结果揭示了哺乳动物增强子的可塑性如何与其进化相交织，并推进了一个在核苷酸分辨率下重编程内源CREs活性的框架。
